Super Artemis 1.2.0 brings profile templates, a rebuilt video resolution picker with a custom size dialog, calibrated bitrate sliders with stepping buttons, a custom accent color picker, six native stability fixes ported from moonlight-common-c, and three streaming fixes found on a Galaxy S24 Ultra: picture-in-picture during calls, a clean end when the system takes the hardware decoder, and faster recovery when the network changes.

**Install:** `SuperArtemis-v1.2.0-arm64-v8a.apk` installs as `com.mohitarora.superartemis`. Automatic update tracking is supported through [Obtainium](https://github.com/Arora-Sir/Super-Artemis#super-artemis).

## What's new in 1.2.0

### Streaming and Connectivity
- Picture-in-picture during calls: Home and Recents gestures during a running call or voice chat (WhatsApp, Meet, Zoom, Telegram, phone call) shrink the stream into a picture-in-picture window instead of ending it. Only a ringing phone keeps the stream full screen.
- Decoder taken by another app: when the system gives the hardware video decoder to another app while the stream is in picture-in-picture (MediaCodec error 1101), the stream now ends cleanly with a message and a reconnect offer, instead of a storm of keyframe requests and a crash of the app.
- Network switch recovery: switching from Wi-Fi to another Wi-Fi or to mobile data starts the automatic resume about 1.5 seconds after the change, even with a VPN such as Tailscale active, instead of waiting for the 10 second silence rule.
- Six stability fixes ported from moonlight-common-c: a video frame can no longer grow without a limit from a flood of continuation packets, clearing a POSIX event takes its mutex, a failed audio start no longer closes its socket twice, the frame index is compared as 32-bit, a new stream resets the RTSP encryption counter and the frame drop count, and a full or shutting down queue frees what it could not take.

### Profiles and Settings
- Profile templates: a profile can be marked as the start for new profiles from the Copy profile menu. A new profile then starts from the current settings with that profile's options laid over them, and existing profiles never change.
- Video resolution picker: standard resolutions are an even grid with the shared ratio in the heading, native display sizes and a Custom resolution row follow, and the custom size dialog has aspect ratio buttons, width and height fields with stepping buttons, and decoder capability validation.
- Bitrate sliders: a calibrated curve puts the 35 to 40 Mbps sweet spot at the center, with 0.5 Mbps steps below 50 Mbps. Every slider dialog has minus and plus buttons and a number field, and long pressing accelerates the stepping.
- Custom accent color picker: it replaces the app style dialog instead of opening on top of it.
- Settings list: the active Resolution, Frame rate and Bitrate show inline in the title, and long titles wrap to two lines on a phone.

### Input and Devices
- Samsung Book Cover Keyboard touchpads are captured on demand, which restores two-finger scrolling.
- Configurable controller rumble rate limiting prevents Android 14 system server crashes with dense vibration on Bluetooth gamepads and DualSense controllers.
- Amlogic Codec2 HEVC decoders on S905X5, S905X5M and S905Y4 TV devices no longer show a slideshow.
- Official PowerA Pro controllers for Nintendo Switch are recognized.
- Physical Japanese JIS keyboards map their language keys to Windows virtual keys for host IME switching.

### Fixes
- The Stream closed reconnect dialog fits the screen in portrait right after a landscape stream.
- The quick bars no longer dim or hide while a finger is on the stream.
- No hard white lines in the Quick-action bars editor on a tablet, and the 1080p entry stays in the resolution picker when the saved custom size is also 1920 by 1080.
- The Copy profile menu stays on screen on a phone, and long Settings titles with a switch wrap instead of being cut off.
